name: SoccerLens
description: SoccerLens is a soccer broadcast video dataset providing per-second bounding box annotations for on-screen graphical overlays (labels and visual cues) alongside natural language commentary. It contains 2,209 annotated frames drawn from 200 soccer match clips, with 4,687 bounding box annotations across three categories: Primary Cue, Secondary Cue, and Common Cue. Each video clip is paired with a match commentary caption and an anonymized version that masks player and team names.
rai:dataLimitations: SoccerLens covers 200 clips from a single data provider (SoccerNet) spanning a limited set of European leagues and seasons (2014–2019). Broadcast angle, resolution, and overlay styles vary by broadcaster and may not generalise to other soccer feeds, sports, or non-broadcast video. The dataset does not include audio or temporal context beyond isolated one-second frames.
rai:dataBiases: Clips were sampled from SoccerNet and may over-represent top-tier European leagues (Bundesliga, Premier League, La Liga, Serie A, Ligue 1). Commentary text reflects the perspective and potential biases of original broadcast commentators. Anonymization replaces only player and team name entities and may miss other identifying references.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Original commentary sentences contain real player and team names sourced from public broadcast commentary. An anonymized version is provided in which all player names are replaced with [PLAYER] and team names with [TEAM]. No other personal or sensitive information (e.g. biometrics, faces, locations of individuals) is included.
rai:dataUseCases: Intended use cases include: (1) training and evaluating object detection models for soccer broadcast overlay elements; (2) explainability research on vision-language models applied to sports video; (3) benchmarking attribution/saliency methods on annotated broadcast frames. Not intended for player identification, surveillance, or any use that re-identifies individuals from anonymized data.
rai:dataSocialImpact: SoccerLens supports research on explainable AI for sports analytics, which can improve transparency of automated video understanding systems used in media and broadcasting. Potential negative impacts are limited given the public-broadcast origin of the data; however, re-identification of anonymized commentary or misuse for player tracking would be inappropriate uses.
prov:wasGeneratedBy: Bounding box annotations were created by human annotators labeling per-second keyframes extracted from SoccerNet broadcast video clips. Commentary text is derived from the SoccerNet commentary dataset. Anonymization was performed with a named-entity replacement script.

distribution.name: annotations-coco.json
distribution.description: COCO-format bounding box annotations for 2,209 annotated video frames across 200 soccer match clips. Contains info, images, annotations, and categories fields following the MS-COCO object detection format.

distribution.name: selected_videos_for_annotations.json
distribution.description: Metadata for the 200 annotated soccer match video clips, including the video path, action caption, broadcast commentary text, anonymized commentary text, league name, and match identifier.

recordSet.name: categories
recordSet.description: Annotation category definitions used in the bounding box annotations.

field.name: id
field.description: Integer category identifier.

field.name: name
field.description: Category name. One of: 'Primary Cue', 'Secondary Cue', 'Common Cue'.

recordSet.name: images
recordSet.description: Metadata for each annotated video frame (treated as an image in COCO format). Frames are extracted at one-second intervals from broadcast soccer video at 1280×720 resolution.

field.name: id
field.description: Unique frame identifier composed of the video path and the second index (e.g. 'league/match/clip.mp4_7').

field.name: file_name
field.description: Relative path to the JPEG frame file.

field.name: video_id
field.description: Relative path of the source video clip.

field.name: second
field.description: Timestamp (in seconds) within the video clip at which the frame was extracted.

field.name: width
field.description: Frame width in pixels (1280).

field.name: height
field.description: Frame height in pixels (720).

recordSet.name: annotations
recordSet.description: Bounding box annotations in COCO format. Each annotation links a frame to a category and provides an axis-aligned bounding box in [x, y, width, height] format with pixel coordinates.

field.name: id
field.description: Unique annotation identifier.

field.name: image_id
field.description: Identifier of the frame this annotation belongs to. References images/id.

field.name: category_id
field.description: Category of the annotated object. References categories/id.

field.name: bbox
field.description: Axis-aligned bounding box in COCO format: [x_min, y_min, width, height] in pixel coordinates.

field.name: iscrowd
field.description: COCO iscrowd flag (0 for all annotations in this dataset).

field.name: no_roi
field.description: Boolean flag indicating whether the annotation has no region of interest.

field.name: label
field.description: Human-readable category label string.

recordSet.name: videos
recordSet.description: Metadata for the 200 annotated soccer match video clips, including action caption, broadcast commentary, and match context.

field.name: video
field.description: Relative path of the video clip (league/match/clip.mp4).

field.name: caption
field.description: Short action label for the clip (e.g. 'corner', 'goal', 'offside').

field.name: comments_text
field.description: Original broadcast commentary sentence describing the action, including player and team names.

field.name: comments_text_anonymized
field.description: Anonymized commentary sentence with player names replaced by [PLAYER] and team names replaced by [TEAM].

field.name: league
field.description: League and season identifier (e.g. 'germany_bundesliga_2016-2017').

field.name: match
field.description: Match identifier including date, time, and teams (e.g. '2016-10-01 - 19-30 Bayer Leverkusen 2 - 0 Dortmund').
